title: Cutover staffing Gantt and release notes skeleton
content:
Purpose / elevator:
This is a compact preflight + staffing Gantt and a lightweight release-notes skeleton for the May sprint ship. Use this when we have a short (24–48h) cutover window that requires explicit cross-team staffing, telemetry checkpoints, and a concise public-facing notes draft.

What this file is NOT: full runbook. It's the crew roster, timed handoffs, and the quick release-notes that product/marketing can iterate from. Keep it short and copyable.

High-level goals:
- Safety first: keep canary small and observable, ready to throttle back to 0% quickly.
- Predictable latency profile during the first 3 hours after cutover.
- Clear on-call and escalation ladder for infra, runtime, and model-routing.
- Draft public release notes that are accurate but minimal.

Quick context:
- Target: deploy feature flag + model-routing update + minor schema change to /v1/generate.
- Canary traffic: start at 0.5% for 30m, then step to 2% for 60m, then 10% for 60m if signals are green.
- Primary telemetry: 95th/99th latency, error rate, tail GPU OOMs, KV-cache hit rate, model-resp-quality regressions (small eval set).

Staffing Gantt (compact timeline, local times PT):
- T-24h (Day -1) => Staffing: Release lead + Eng oncall + SRE primary; prep checklist done. Owners: Maya (release lead), Diego (SRE), Priya (serving runtime).
- T-3h => Preflight smoke on staging (smoke ticket + perf baseline), push alerting thresholds. Owners: Priya, Evan.
- T-30m => Crew huddle (15m): confirm rollback steps and comm channel (#deploys-ops). All on-call and shift leads.
- T=0 (cutover start) 00:00 PT => Apply db migration toggle + config flip for model routing; deploy artifact to canary nodes only. Owners: release lead + infra deployer.
- T+30m => Canary check-1: if error rate < 0.1% and 95p latency within +20% of baseline, step to 2%. Owner: SRE primary.
- T+90m => Canary check-2: run embedded quality eval set (10 prompts) against production canary outputs; if A/B metrics stable, step to 10%. Owner: Applied ML contact.
- T+150m => Full monitor window; if signals ok, open for gradual ramp per traffic policy.
- T+180m => Release notes finalization and notify product/marketing.

Callouts for each role (short):
- Release lead (Maya): final go/no-go, comms (hipchat + email digest), coordinate rollback.
- SRE (Diego): threshold tuning, traffic throttles, immediate rollback authority if infra signals.
- Serving runtime (Priya): watch KV cache, GPU memory, batching latencies; hotfix deploy path ready.
- Applied ML (Evan): run small eval harness, watch embedding similarity regressions and hallucination flags.
- Observability (TBD): ensure dashboards are pinned and sampling increased for the first 3 hours.

Smoke & preflight checklist (must be green before T-0):
- [ ] Canary artifact built and validated in CI (CI job green, PR merged).
- [ ] Feature flags created and validated (featureflag/ui link).
- [ ] Staging smoke run completed: baseline latencies captured and compared.
- [ ] Alerts deployed with thresholds and docs updated.
- [ ] Rollback artifact and config known + tested in staging.
- [ ] Pager rotations updated, Slack channel pinned with runbook.
- [ ] Dependency verification: model weights present on canary hosts, KMS access validated.

Fast rollback ladder (short):
1) Toggle feature flag back to previous variant (instant).
2) If toggle fails, deploy previous artifact to canary nodes (5–10m).
3) If broader degradation, evacuate traffic to the standby region and revert routing policy (requires SRE).

Simple decision matrix (minutes):
- Latency spike >50% sustained 5m => step down traffic to previous tier, SRE investigate.
- Error rate >0.5% sustained 5m => rollback to 0% canary immediately.
- GPU OOM or memory thrash => pause rollout and escalate to serving runtime.

Telemetry quick-links (attach to ticket before T-0):
- Latency dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood/boards/latency-cutover-may2027
- Error grouping: https://sentry.redwood/projects/platform/issues?query=cutover
- Canary output eval harness: https://ci.redwood/job/canary-eval/982

Release notes draft (public-facing, keep minimal):
- Title: "May 2027: Targeted model-routing update and GFE latency improvements"
- TL;DR: Deployed targeted routing for reduced tail-latency for small-sequence workloads; no user-facing breaking changes expected.
- What changed (bullets):
  - Adjusted model-routing policy to prefer low-latency quantized variants for short requests.
  - Minor schema relax for optional metadata on /v1/generate (backwards compatible).
  - Backend batching improvements to reduce small-request 95p by ~10–15%.
- Who should care: platform partners using high-QPS low-latency flows; contact eng-release-engineering@redwood.com for questions.
- Rollback plan: full rollback option available and will be executed if latency or error regressions exceed defined thresholds.
- Known issues: small subset of embedding jobs may see slightly higher variance for very long sequences during rollout ramp. We will monitor for 24h.

Internal release notes (more detail for SEs & support):
- Migration: no DB migrations that require downtime; feature flag controls routing logic.
- Observability: increased sampling to 5% for first 3h; eval harness will run every 60m during canary.
- Telemetry to verify: 95p latency, 99p latency, error-rate by model variant, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate.

Open questions / TODOs before cutover:
- Who is the named observability lead for first 3h? (assign by EOD T-1).
- Confirm marketing copy ownership for the public notes (suggest: product-ops).
- Confirm SLO guardrail numbers to apply for this rollout window (SRE to publish).

Post-cutover checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] 1h digest: capture basic metrics and any anomalies, send to #deploys-ops.
- [ ] 3h digest: detailed telemetry and canary eval outputs.
- [ ] 24h retrospective (async): short blameless notes in the ticket and a follow-up action items list.

Retrospective prompts (for after):
- Did our canary step durations match the runbook? If not, why?
- Any false positive/negative triggers in alerts?
- Were staffing rotations sufficient during the window?
- What could automation do next time to reduce manual handoffs?

Quick snippets to paste into PR / ticket (copyable):
- Canary plan: "0.5% (30m) -> 2% (60m) -> 10% (60m). Stepdown criteria: steady-state error rate >0.5% or latency 95p > +20% baseline sustained 5m."
- Rollback: "Feature-flag toggle rollback (primary) -> deploy previous artifact to canaries (secondary) -> region evacuation (tertiary)."

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep the release notes short — product will add customer-facing language.
- Make sure to pin the latency dashboard in the deploy ticket and increase sampling before cutover.
- Remind Applied ML to run the 10-prompt eval at T+90m (script is in the linked CI job).

---
Edit history / quick log:
- 2027-05-02: initial sketch and staffing Gantt (Maya).
- 2027-05-03: added SRE thresholds and rollback ladder (Diego).
- 2027-05-04: added release-notes skeleton and observability links (Priya).

If anything is unclear ping Maya in Slack (@mayachen) or add a quick note in the ticket JIRA-8712.
